key_insight: Scalable modal analysis identifies dominant coherent flow structures and their temporal dynamics around a Formula 1 front wing while compressing approximately 6 TB of snapshots into 200 GB of modal data.
engineering_relevance: Linking aerodynamic structures to characteristic frequencies can help engineers interpret unsteady front-wing flow and manage large simulation datasets.
method: Simulate the Imperial Front Wing at Re = 2.2 × 10^5 using Nektar++ spectral/hp-element LES with 49.72 million degrees of freedom.
Apply scalable POD and DMD through the open-source pyLOM framework.
Associate DMD modes with flow mechanisms using point-probe spectra.
evidence_signal: Mean lift and drag coefficients differ from reference data by 2.24% and 2.87%, respectively; modes at chord-based Strouhal numbers 5.1, 7.5 and 9.3 are associated with separation-bubble dynamics, canard-vortex pulsation and endplate-vortex meander.
watch_item: The abstract demonstrates one geometry and Reynolds number; generalization to other operating conditions remains unestablished.
paper_title: Scalable Modal Analysis of the Imperial Front Wing Flow Field
